questions.q: For the relation R(A, B, C, D, E) with F = {A → B, B → C, CD → E}, the attribute closure A⁺ is
questions.e: A gives B, B gives C, so we have {A, B, C}. CD → E needs D, which is not in the closure, so E is not added.

questions.q: Relation R is decomposed into R1 and R2. The decomposition is lossless if the common attributes of R1 and R2
o: form a superkey of R1 or of R2
form a foreign key of R
questions.e: The lossless-join test requires R1 ∩ R2 → R1 or R1 ∩ R2 → R2, that is, the common attributes must be a superkey of at least one of the two parts.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about SQL joins.
I. An inner join returns the unmatched rows of both tables.
II. A left outer join returns all rows of the left table, with NULLs in the right-table columns where no match exists.
Which of the above is/are correct?
questions.e: II is true. I is false: an inner join returns only the rows that satisfy the join condition, so unmatched rows of either table are dropped.

questions.q: For the relation Emp shown, how many rows are returned by `SELECT eid FROM Emp WHERE sal > (SELECT AVG(sal) FROM Emp);`?
questions.e: The average salary is (10 + 20 + 30 + 40 + 60) / 5 = 32. Only 40 and 60 are above it, so 2 rows.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a fundamental operator of relational algebra?
questions.e: The fundamental operators are select, project, union, set difference, Cartesian product and rename. Natural join is a derived operator, expressible using Cartesian product, selection and projection.

questions.q:
Transactions T1, T2 and T3 have timestamps 10, 20 and 30. Under basic timestamp ordering, the following operations arrive in order:
r1(X), w2(X), r3(X), w1(X), w3(Y), r1(Y), w2(Y)
The transactions rolled back are
questions.e: w1(X) fails because R-TS(X) = 30 > 10, so T1 is aborted. Then w3(Y) sets W-TS(Y) = 30. T2's write on Y has TS 20 < 30, so T2 is aborted too. T1's later r1(Y) is not executed.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about a relation.
I. The degree of a relation is its number of attributes.
II. The cardinality of a relation is its number of tuples.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Both are true. Degree counts the columns (attributes) and cardinality counts the rows (tuples).

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about SQL views.
I. A view permanently stores its own copy of the data.
II. A view cannot be created from another view.
Which of the above is/are correct?
questions.e: A view is a virtual relation defined by a query and normally stores no data of its own, so I is false. A view can be defined over other views, so II is also false.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements.
I. Two-phase locking guarantees conflict serialisable schedules.
II. Strict two-phase locking avoids cascading rollbacks.
Which of the above is/are correct?
questions.e: Any schedule allowed by 2PL is conflict serialisable. Strict 2PL holds exclusive locks until commit or abort, so no transaction reads uncommitted data and cascading rollback is avoided.

questions.q: In basic timestamp ordering, transaction T with timestamp TS(T) issues write(Q), and the read timestamp of Q is greater than TS(T). What happens?
o: T waits until Q is unlocked
questions.e: A younger transaction has already read Q, so T's write would invalidate that read. The write is rejected and T is rolled back. Ignoring the write is the Thomas write rule, used only when the write timestamp is larger.

questions.q: For R(A, B, C, D) with functional dependencies AB → C, C → D and D → A, the number of candidate keys is
questions.e: AB⁺, BC⁺ and BD⁺ each give all attributes, and no single attribute does. B is in every key, and the minimal keys are AB, BC and BD.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT one of Armstrong's three basic axioms for functional dependencies?
questions.e: Armstrong's axioms are reflexivity, augmentation and transitivity. Union (if X → Y and X → Z then X → YZ) is a derived rule, proved from those three.

questions.q: For the relation T shown, what is the output of `SELECT COUNT(*), COUNT(Marks), AVG(Marks) FROM T;`?
questions.e: COUNT(*) counts all 4 rows, COUNT(Marks) skips the NULL and gives 3, and AVG ignores NULL: (10 + 20 + 30) / 3 = 20.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about transaction control in SQL.
I. ROLLBACK undoes the changes made by the current uncommitted transaction.
II. ROLLBACK can undo the changes of a transaction that has already been committed.
Which of the above is/are correct?
questions.e: I is true. II is false: once COMMIT has made the changes permanent, ROLLBACK cannot reverse them. It only affects work done since the last commit.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a level of the three-schema architecture?
questions.e: The three levels are the internal (physical), conceptual (logical) and external (view) schemas. There is no procedural schema level.

questions.q: A block holds 1024 bytes. In a B+ tree, the search key is 10 bytes and a block pointer is 6 bytes. If an internal node holds n pointers and n − 1 keys, the largest n that fits in one block is
questions.e: We need 6n + 10(n − 1) ≤ 1024, so 16n ≤ 1034 and n ≤ 64.6. The largest integer is 64.

questions.q:
Regarding the two-phase locking (2PL) protocol, consider the following.
I. In the shrinking phase, a transaction may still acquire new locks.
II. 2PL ensures conflict serialisability of schedules.
Which of the above is/are correct?
questions.e: II is true. I is false: the shrinking phase begins when the first lock is released, and from then on the transaction may only release locks, never acquire new ones.

questions.q: Match the normal form in List I with the condition it enforces in List II.

head: List I
List II
rows: 2. No transitive dependency of a non-prime attribute on a key
4. No partial dependency on a candidate key

questions.e: 1NF needs atomic values, 2NF removes partial dependency on a key, 3NF removes transitive dependency of non-prime attributes, and BCNF needs every determinant to be a superkey.

questions.q: The relation Emp is shown. What is the output of `SELECT SUM(salary) FROM Emp WHERE dept = 'HR';`?
questions.e: HR rows have salaries 30000 and 25000, which add up to 55000.

questions.q: For R(A, B, C, D, E) with F = {AB → C, B → D, C → E}, the highest normal form of R is
questions.e: The only candidate key is AB. D is non-prime and depends on B, a proper part of the key, which is a partial dependency. So 2NF is violated and R is only in 1NF.

questions.q: A file has 30000 fixed-length records of 100 bytes each, stored unspanned in blocks of 1024 bytes and ordered on a key. A sparse primary index has one entry of 16 bytes per data block. Using binary search on the index, the number of block accesses to find a record is
questions.e: Blocking factor is 10, so there are 3000 data blocks. The index entry count is 3000 with 64 entries per block, so 47 index blocks. Binary search takes ⌈log₂47⌉ = 6, plus 1 data block access gives 7.

questions.q: In a distributed database, dividing a relation into subsets of tuples that are stored at different sites is called
questions.e: Horizontal fragmentation splits by rows, while vertical fragmentation splits by columns. Replication keeps copies of the data at several sites.

questions.q: The relation P(eid, sal) has the rows (1, 50), (2, 80), (3, 80), (4, 60), (5, 30). What does the following query return?
questions.code:
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM P e
WHERE 2 > (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT sal)
           FROM P
           WHERE sal > e.sal);
questions.e: For each row it counts the distinct salaries higher than its own. Both 80s give 0 and 60 gives 1, so they qualify (count < 2). 50 gives 2 and 30 gives 3, so they do not. The result is 3.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a DML command?
questions.e: CREATE defines a schema object and so belongs to DDL. INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE manipulate the data and are DML.

questions.q: After a crash, the recovery manager finds <T1, start> in the log but no <T1, commit>. Under immediate-update log-based recovery, T1 is
o: undone using old values in the log
redone using new values in the log
questions.e: An incomplete transaction may have written to the database, so its updates are undone using the old values. Transactions with a commit record are redone.
